Hi Alex,

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. Quick hits below and I've attached a couple artifacts to start: dataflow_v2.svg (visual), subprocessor_list_202605.pdf (export from our registry).

- Data flow: Primary ingestion goes to a customer-dedicated ingestion tier and is written to encrypted S3 buckets (region selectable). We use an in-memory KV cache for short-lived session state (default TTL 10m); cache contents are not persisted to disk. See attached dataflow_v2.svg for the diagram.

- Subprocessors: attached PDF lists infra (AWS), logging/observability provider, metrics pipeline, and a small set of analytics vendors. We call out whether each processor sees unencrypted payloads on the list.

- KMS/keys: For Hosted Redwood API we manage keys via AWS KMS. For Dedicated and Private deployments we offer options: dedicated KMS integration and customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments. There are some contractual and technical caveats for CMK — Laura can add the legal language.

- Access controls: Role-based access with least privilege. Admins and SREs require MFA + JIT approval for sensitive operations. We maintain operator access logs and tie console actions to identities via SSO (OIDC/SAML) and an approval workflow for sensitive read operations.

- Retention: Default audit/trace log retention in Console is 90 days. Enterprise customers can request extended retention (custom contract). We can also provide filtered export of audit logs for customer audits.

Next steps: Laura (legal) and Grace (solutions/security) are looped to provide the contractual language and any deeper implementation notes. If it's helpful I can set a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the diagram and answers.

Hi all — Laura from Legal. Quick answers and suggested contract language below; I've attached a short DPA addendum PDF for signature.

1) Customer-managed keys: 
- Private deployments: full support for BYOK/CMK (customer supplies key material via supported HSM/KMS; Redwood will not retain plaintext key material).
- Dedicated deployments: we support customer-managed keys integrated with customer KMS in many configurations; for some managed Dedicated offerings we maintain the KMS root and provide a KMS-handover plan. Specifics go in the DPA addendum.

Suggested contract snippet: "Customer may provision and manage encryption keys for Customer Data; Redwood will not export or retain key material provided by Customer and will use Customer keys to encrypt Customer Data at rest where technically supported. Any key escrow or recovery mechanism will be subject to separate written agreement."

2) KV cache and persistence: 
- By design the in-memory KV cache is ephemeral (default TTL 10m) and not written to durable storage. We can provide a config that disables caching of PII fields and log masking rules to ensure PII is not present in observability exports.

Suggested contract snippet: "Redwood represents that ephemeral caches used by the Service do not persist Customer Data to durable repositories and that logging/observability exports will be subject to agreed masking rules for personally identifying data."

3) Audit logs / deletion certification: 
- Default retention 90 days. For customers requesting shorter retention for specific data classes, Redwood can produce deletion confirmation reports and export logs for customer audit on request; for longer retention we offer a contractual option.

Suggested contract snippet: "Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide a written confirmation describing the actions taken to delete Customer Data from operational systems and will provide exports of audit logs relevant to the request. Extended retention or bespoke deletion guarantees will be addressed in a written addendum."

I've attached redwood_dpa_addendum_20260523.pdf which includes the CMK language and audit log options. If that looks good we can send a DocuSign link — provisioned here: https://docusign.com/rf/ProspectCorp-DPA-Addendum-20260523 (expires in 7 days).
